name: Splenic Architecture and Overwhelming Postsplenectomy Infection

reference.source: ALGrawany Anatomy & Physiology Made Easy 2026 / Sabiston Surgery 22e
clinicalPearls: Spleen lies in left hypochondrium under ribs 9-11; suspensory ligaments carry short gastric and splenic vessels
White pulp synthesizes opsonizing antibodies and houses B and T lymphocytes
Red pulp cords of Billroth filter aged, non-deformable erythrocytes through 2-micrometer endothelial slits
Overwhelming postsplenectomy infection (OPSI) is caused by encapsulated bacteria: S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae
Postsplenectomy blood film reveals Howell-Jolly bodies (nuclear DNA remnants), Heinz bodies, and target cells
reference.pathophysiology: The spleen acts as a lymphoid immune organ and mechanical erythrocyte filter. In the red pulp, sinusoids test red cell deformability. In the white pulp, marginal zone B-cells generate IgM against bacterial capsular polysaccharide antigens. Splenectomy impairs opsonization, predisposing to fulminant bacteremia and septic shock.
additionalDifferentials: Splenic rupture following blunt abdominal trauma
Splenic infarction in sickle cell disease
additionalInvestigations: Complete blood count with peripheral smear examination for Howell-Jolly bodies
Abdominal ultrasound or CT to evaluate splenic trauma or splenomegaly
Blood cultures in any febrile asplenic patient
